Memo submitted. Here's the bottom line:

## US March 2026 Revenue by Stream

| Stream | GL | USD |
|---|---|---|
| Subscription | 4000 | 52,300.00 |
| Usage | 4100 | 977.00 |
| Professional Services | 4200 | 7,500.00 |
| **Total** | | **60,777.00** |

**The trail** — eight ledger entries, all posted and all with support attached:

- **Subscription**: five 3/01 invoices (Acme 18,000 / Corvid 11,500 / Fairview 9,400 / Beacon 8,000 / Evergreen 6,200 = 53,100 gross) less JE-00275, an 800.00 SLA credit memo to Beacon Health. Entries JE-00215, 219, 222, 224, 225, 275.
- **Usage**: JE-00236 alone, 977.00 (Acme, INV-2180).
- **Professional Services**: JE-00255 alone, 7,500.00 (Fairview implementation, INV-2118).

Nothing was changed in the books — no entries posted, reversed, or modified, and no checklist items touched.

**One thing you should know before quoting the usage number.** INV-2180 is dated 3/04 but describes *"API usage overage – February 2026 (billed in arrears)"* — and February already carries INV-2120 for 844.00, also labeled February usage. So either the 977.00 is a February-service item sitting in March with no March usage billed or accrued at all, or February got billed twice. The differing amounts suggest a true-up or a sloppy invoice description rather than a clean duplicate, but there's no usage report or contract billing term in the document store to settle it. I did not force an adjustment; I logged it as **EXC-001** for the revenue accountant to confirm the Acme billing convention.

Practically: **subscription + professional services of 59,800.00 is fully defensible today**; the 977.00 usage line is provisional. The exposure is capped at 1.6% of the total.

Two supporting points that gave me comfort on completeness: I searched all US March customer invoices and credit memos — eight exist, eight are booked, none missing. And Deferred Revenue and Unbilled Receivables are both zero with zero activity, so revenue is purely invoice-driven. That second point cuts both ways, though — it also means there's no accrual mechanism in place to pick up unbilled March usage, which is exactly why EXC-001 matters rather than being a cosmetic labeling nit.
